recipes.name: MONKEY BREAD
ingredients: For the Monte Cristo Monkey Bread
85 g unsalted butter, cubed + very soft (~75 80 °F)
For the Herb Garlic Monkey Bread
85 g unsalted butter, cubed + very soft (~75 80 °F)
stick As needed cooking olive oil or non spray
For the Cinnamon Sugar Monkey Bread
170 g granulated sugar, divided + more for the pan
85 g unsalted butter, cubed + very soft (~75 80 °F)
instructions: For the Monte Cristo Monkey Bread
Combine the flour, yeast, and sugar in the bowl of a stand mixer. - 500 g bread flour - 7 g instant dry yeast - 50 g granulated sugar
Evenly combine the dry ingredients using a whisk or fork.

Add the milk, water, and salt to the bowl. With the mixer fitted with a dough hook attachment, combine the dough on medium-low speed until almost homogeneous. - 100 g whole milk warm (~85 °F) - 200 g water warm (~85 °F) - 7 g kosher salt

Begin adding the butter, one cube at a time, and waiting until each cube is incorporated before adding another one until all of the butter has been added. - 85 g unsalted butter cubed + very soft (~75 80 °F)
Increase the speed to medium-high and mix until the dough is smooth, elastic, and clears the sides of the bowl, about 6-8 minutes.
Transfer the dough to a large greased bowl and cover it with plastic wrap.
Let the dough proof until about doubled in size, about 1-2 hours depending on the warmth of the room.
Meanwhile, grease 1 large tube or bundt pan or loaf pan or muffin tin generously with non-stick spray. - As needed non spray
In a small bowl, combine the ham and cheese. Toss to combine. - Deli ham (preferably honey ham) sliced - Gruyere cheese grated
Remove the dough from the bowl and place it on a lightly oiled work surface. Divide and shape the dough into even golf-ball-sized portions. *If using a muffin tin, make portions half the size.
Roll the dough balls in the melted butter and then in the ham and cheese mixture. Place them into the prepared baking pan(s).
Loosely cover the pan(s), and allow the dough to proof for another 45 minutes - 1 hour, until puffed.
Meanwhile, preheat the oven to 350°F.
Once risen, remove the plastic wrap from the pan(s).
Bake the monkey bread for 30-35 minutes, turning halfway through, until the dough is cooked through (200-205°F) and golden brown on top.
Allow the bread to cool for 10 minutes, then flip it onto a serving platter of your choice. Serve warm with a sprinkle of powdered sugar and jam. - Powdered sugar - Raspberry jam
For the Herb Garlic Monkey Bread
Combine the flour, yeast, and sugar in the bowl of a stand mixer. - 500 g bread flour - 7 g instant dry yeast - 50 g granulated sugar
Evenly combine the dry ingredients using a whisk or fork.

Add the milk, water, and salt to the bowl. With the mixer fitted with a dough hook attachment, combine the dough on medium-low speed until almost homogeneous. - 100 g whole milk warm (~85 °F) - 200 g water warm (~85 °F) - 10 g kosher salt

Begin adding the butter, one cube at a time, and waiting until each cube is incorporated before adding another one until all of the butter has been added. - 85 g unsalted butter cubed + very soft (~75 80 °F)
Increase the speed to medium-high and mix until the dough is smooth, elastic, and clears the sides of the bowl, about 4-5 minutes.
Transfer the dough to a large greased bowl and cover it with plastic wrap.
Let the dough proof until about doubled in size, about 1-2 hours depending on the warmth of the room.
Meanwhile, grease 1 large tube or bundt pan or loaf pan or muffin tin generously with non-stick spray. - As needed cooking olive oil or non spray
Remove the dough from the bowl and place it on a lightly oiled work surface. Divide and shape the dough into even golf-ball-sized portions.*If using a muffin tin, make portions half the size.

Roll the dough balls in a mixture of the melted butter, fresh herbs (of your choice), salt, and pepper. Place them into the prepared baking pan(s). - Melted unsalted butter - Parsley chopped - Chives chopped - Dill chopped - Garlic minced - Kosher salt - Freshly ground black pepper
Loosely cover the pan(s), and allow the dough to proof for another 45 minutes - 1 hour, until puffed.
Meanwhile, preheat the oven to 350°F.
Once risen, remove the plastic wrap from the pan(s).
Bake the monkey bread for 30-35 minutes, turning halfway through, until the dough is cooked through (200-205 °F) and golden brown on top.
Allow the bread to cool for 10 minutes, then flip it onto a serving platter of your choice. Brush the dough with any remaining herb butter. Serve warm.
For the Cinnamon Sugar Monkey Bread
Combine the flour, yeast, and 50 grams of sugar in the bowl of a stand mixer. - 500 g bread flour - 7 g instant dry yeast - 50 g granulated sugar divided + more for the pan
Evenly combine the dry ingredients using a whisk or fork.

Add the milk, water, and salt to the bowl. With the mixer fitted with a dough hook attachment, combine the dough on medium-low speed until almost homogeneous. - 100 g whole milk warm (~85 °F) - 200 g water warm (~85 °F) - 10 g kosher salt

Begin adding the butter, one cube at a time, and waiting until each cube is incorporated before adding another one until all of the butter has been added. - 85 g unsalted butter cubed + very soft (~75 80 °F)
Increase the speed to medium-high and mix until the dough is smooth, elastic, and clears the sides of the bowl, about 4-5 minutes.
Transfer the dough to a large greased bowl and cover it with plastic wrap.
Let the dough proof until about doubled in size, about 1-2 hours depending on the warmth of the room.
Meanwhile, grease 1 large tube or bundt pan or loaf pan or muffin tin generously with non-stick spray. - As needed non spray
In a small bowl, combine the granulated sugar, brown sugar, and cinnamon. Whisk to combine. - 120 g granulated sugar divided + more for the pan - 200 g brown sugar - 2 tbsp cinnamon
Remove the dough from the bowl and place it on a lightly oiled work surface. Divide and shape the dough into even golf-ball-sized portions.*If using a muffin tin, make portions half the size.
Roll the dough balls in the melted butter and then in the cinnamon-sugar mixture. Place them into the prepared baking pan(s).
Loosely cover the pan(s), and allow the dough to proof for another 45 minutes - 1 hour, until puffed.
Meanwhile, preheat the oven to 350°F.
Once risen, remove the plastic wrap from the pan(s). Brush the dough with any remaining cinnamon-sugar mixture.
Bake the monkey bread for 30-35 minutes, turning halfway through, until the dough is cooked through (200-205°F) and golden brown on top.
Allow the bread to cool for 10 minutes, then flip it onto a serving platter of your choice.
